sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and router setup
sections.what: Brings in the router, file response type, request checking, the database session and the UUID type.
sections.why: Likely reason: the endpoints below need these tools.
sections.watch_out: The file response type is imported but not used, which suggests the download is still to be built.

sections.name: ExportRequest
sections.title: Export request shape
sections.what: Describes what a caller sends: project ID, export type, and two yes or no options for citations and run IDs.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the caller choose how much traceability detail to include.
sections.watch_out: The export type is free text. The comment lists allowed values, but nothing enforces them.

sections.name: ExportResponse
sections.title: Export reply shape
sections.what: Describes the reply with an export ID, file name, size and citation count.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives the caller what it needs to fetch the file.
sections.watch_out: The reply has no download address, so a caller cannot find the file from this reply alone.

sections.name: create_export
sections.title: Create export endpoint
sections.what: Accepts an export request and returns a fixed ID, a file name built from the requested type, a size of about one megabyte and 45 citations. No file is created.
sections.why: Likely reason: a placeholder. The docstring describes the intended report content.
sections.watch_out: The ID is always the same, so repeated requests return the same export ID.

sections.name: download_export
sections.title: Download export endpoint
sections.what: Accepts an export ID and always returns a message that download is not yet implemented, with status 501.
sections.why: Likely reason: a placeholder until file storage and serving are written. The code comment says so.
sections.watch_out: Every ID gets the same message, so a caller cannot tell a missing export from an unbuilt feature.

summary: Exposes endpoints to request an export file and to download one, and both are placeholders.
purpose: Lets a caller ask for a PowerPoint, Excel, CSV or JSON export of a project and fetch it later.
why: Likely reason: the routes are set up before file generation is written. The download comment says so.
how: 1) Create takes the project, export type and two include options. 2) It returns a made-up file name and size. 3) Download returns a not-implemented message with status 501.
inputs: Project ID, export type and two yes or no options.
outputs: A reply with an ID, file name, size and citation count, or a 501 message.
risks: Create returns a file name and size for a file that is never made, so a caller may think a file exists. The include options have no effect. The export type is not checked against the allowed list.
debug: If downloads return 501, the download feature is not built yet. If a file name looks fake, the create placeholder is still active.
